t.6.49.1: Then the mighty Rāma, of great splendor, taking up his bow, beheld Kumbhakarṇa, the crowned one of enormous body.
t.6.49.2: Seeing that foremost of rākṣasas, mountain-like in appearance, like the lord Nārāyaṇa of old striding across the sky,
t.6.49.3: Seeing him, who resembled a cloud laden with water and was adorned with golden armlets, the great army of the monkeys fled once more.
t.6.49.4: Seeing the army fleeing and the rākṣasa growing ever larger, Rāma, filled with astonishment, spoke these words to Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.6.49.5: Who is that hero, like a mountain, crowned with a diadem, with tawny eyes, who is seen in Laṅkā like a rain-cloud with lightning?
t.6.49.6: That one huge being seen here stands like a banner of the earth; seeing him, all the monkeys flee in every direction.
t.6.49.8: Thus questioned by the prince Rāma, whose deeds are accomplished without strain, the greatly wise Vibhīṣaṇa spoke these words to Kākutstha.
t.6.49.7: Tell me, who is that huge one? Is he a rākṣasa or an asura? Never before have I seen a creature of this kind.
t.6.49.9: He by whom Vaivasvata and Vāsava were vanquished in battle, that very one is this mighty Kumbhakarṇa, the son of Viśravas.
t.6.49.11: The thirty gods were unable to slay the mighty Kumbhakarṇa, spear in hand and hideous-eyed, for they were bewildered, thinking, "This is Death himself."
t.6.49.10: By him, O Rāghava, the Devas in battle, and the Dānavas, the Yakṣas, the serpents and the flesh-eaters, and the Gandharvas, Vidyādharas and Kiṃnaras have been routed by the thousands.
t.6.49.12: For this Kumbhakarṇa is by his very nature full of splendour and mighty in strength, whereas the strength of the other lords of the rākṣasas has been produced by the granting of boons.
t.6.49.13: As soon as he was born, this mighty one, tormented by hunger, devoured many thousands of living creatures.
t.6.49.14: As they were being devoured, the creatures, oppressed by fear, went to Śakra for refuge and also reported that matter to him.
t.6.49.15: Enraged, the great Indra, wielder of the thunderbolt, struck Kumbhakarṇa with his sharp thunderbolt. Struck by Śakra's thunderbolt, the mighty one staggered, and in his fury he roared loudly.
t.6.49.16: Hearing the roar of the wise Kumbhakarṇa as he bellowed again and again, the earth, already terrified, trembled once more.
t.6.49.17: Then, in his rage against Mahendra, the mighty Kumbhakarṇa tore a tusk from Airāvata and struck Vāsava on the chest with it.
t.6.49.19: And Śakra, together with the beings, went to the abode of Svayambhū; they told Prajāpati of Kumbhakarṇa's wickedness, of his devouring of the beings and also of his assault upon the gods.
t.6.49.18: Stricken by Kumbhakarṇa's blow, Vāsava staggered, and at once the gods, the brahmarṣis and the Dānavas were filled with dismay.
t.6.49.20: If he devours living creatures in this way every day, then in a very short time the world will become empty.
t.6.49.21: Having heard the words of Vāsava, the Grandfather of all the worlds summoned the Rākṣasas and saw Kumbhakarṇa.
t.6.49.22: Merely on beholding Kumbhakarṇa, Prajāpati was struck with terror; and having seen him and sighed, the Self-born One spoke these words.
t.6.49.24: Then Rāvaṇa, greatly agitated, spoke these words: "A full-grown golden tree is being cut down at the very time of its fruiting."
t.6.49.23: Surely you have been created by Paulastya for the destruction of the worlds; therefore from this day forward you shall lie like one dead. Then, overpowered by Brahmā's curse, he fell down before the lord.
t.6.49.25: O Prajāpati, it is not right to curse your own great-grandson thus; yet you are not one whose word is false, so he will sleep, there is no doubt. But let a time be fixed for his sleeping and likewise for his waking.
t.6.49.26: Having heard Rāvaṇa's words, Svayambhū said this: "He will indeed sleep for six months and will stay awake for a single day."
t.6.49.27: But this hero, roaming the earth hungry, with his mouth gaping wide, could devour the worlds in a single day, like a fire blazing in fury.
t.6.49.28: That very King Rāvaṇa, having now fallen into calamity and frightened by your valour, has awakened Kumbhakarṇa.
t.6.49.29: This very hero of fearsome valor has come forth from the camp, and, greatly enraged, he runs about devouring the monkeys.
t.6.49.30: At the mere sight of Kumbhakarṇa the monkeys fled in all directions. How will the monkeys hold him back when he is enraged in battle?
t.6.49.31: Let all the monkeys be told, "This is a mechanical contrivance that has been set up." Knowing this, the monkeys will become fearless here.
t.6.49.32: Having heard Vibhīṣaṇa's well-reasoned words, which came forth from his gracious mouth, Rāghava then spoke to Nīla, the commander of the army.
t.6.49.33: Go, marshal all the troops in battle array and take your stand by the fire, seizing the gates of Laṅkā, its roads, and then its bridges as well.
t.6.49.35: Commanded by Rāghava, Nīla, the commander of the monkey host, that elephant among monkeys, directed the army of vānaras in due order.
t.6.49.34: Gathering up mountain peaks, trees and rocks as well, let all the monkeys stand ready, armed, with crags in their hands.
t.6.49.36: Then Gavākṣa, Śarabha, Hanumān, Aṅgada and Nala, themselves like mountains, seized mountain peaks and advanced upon the gate.
t.6.49.37: Then that fierce army of the monkeys, with rocks and trees raised in their hands, shone forth just like a vast and fearsome mass of great rain-clouds gathered close about a mountain.
